summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would limit foreign ownership of Australian agribusiness and land, giving the Treasurer powers to prohibit acquisitions and order interests to be sold.
It would generally cap foreign ownership at 49 per cent for covered agribusinesses and land parcels of at least 4 hectares, subject to an exception.
The Foreign Investment Review Board could permit holdings providing substantial national benefits, while arrangements already in place for at least 12 months would be unaffected.
changes: The Board would assess covered investment proposals and recommend whether they were contrary to the national interest.
The Treasurer could require divestment when an acquisition continued contrary to a prohibition notice.
Anti-avoidance provisions would address multiple acquisitions and adjoining land purchases.
The bill would extend to external Territories.
summary.affected: Foreign persons and bodies, Australian agribusinesses, the Foreign Investment Review Board and the Treasurer are affected.

speeches.speaker: Bob Katter
speeches.brief: Introduced the Australian Ownership Bill 2013 to cap foreign ownership at 49 per cent of Australian agribusinesses or land parcels of four hectares or more, warning Australia is already a net importer of fruit, vegetables, seafood and pork, and noted that of 28 sugar mills nationwide, all but those in Mackay and a small New South Wales operation are now foreign owned, compared with all-Australian ownership sixteen years ago.
